output.title: Decreasing students’ stress through time management training

scenes.narration: University students often feel stressed, and this paper asks whether a short time management training can change that in higher education.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits at a desk surrounded by papers, with a small clock and stress marks around them.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist hand-drawn student at desk with scattered papers, a clock, and orange stress lines, on cream background, black ink line art with orange and yellow accents.

scenes.narration: The authors studied 23 undergraduate students who attended one training and reported demands, perceived stress, and perceived control of time before and after.
scenes.layout_description: Three simple icons show a checklist, a stress gauge, and a clock, linked by arrows.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three labeled icons in a row connected by arrows: checklist, stress gauge, clock, with a student figure beside them.

scenes.narration: They used a non-equivalent dependent variable design, meaning demands should stay unchanged while stress and control of time should shift after training.
scenes.layout_description: A balance-like sketch shows two variables moving and one staying still.
scenes.visual_prompt: A minimalist diagram with two arrows moving upward and downward for stress and control, while a third arrow for demands stays flat.

scenes.narration: The training focused on prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring, all meant to support students’ time management.
scenes.layout_description: Five small symbols form a path from left to right, suggesting steps in a process.
scenes.visual_prompt: A sequence of five simple icons—star, target, ladder, calendar, checklist—arranged as a path.

scenes.narration: Students reflected on their activities, set concrete goals, planned steps, and thought about obstacles and deadlines for their studies.
scenes.layout_description: A student looks at a notebook with arrows pointing from activities to goals and deadlines.
scenes.visual_prompt: Student writing in a notebook with arrows from small activity icons to a target and a deadline mark.

scenes.narration: They also made daily schedules and monitored task completion, so the training linked planning with follow-through in everyday student work.
scenes.layout_description: A calendar page and checklist sit beside a student’s hand holding a pen.
scenes.visual_prompt: A hand-drawn calendar with blocks, a checklist with ticks, and a pen, all in a clean minimalist layout.

scenes.narration: The sample came from a medium-sized German university, and students from all faculties were invited as an extracurricular activity.
scenes.layout_description: A simple campus building sits behind a group of diverse student figures.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal campus building with several student silhouettes and an invitation flyer icon.

scenes.narration: The training lasted 4 h, and questionnaires were filled in directly before training, then 2 weeks later and again 4 weeks later.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline with three marked points runs across the slide.
scenes.visual_prompt: A horizontal timeline with three dots labeled by simple clock icons and arrows showing the sequence.

scenes.narration: For the main analyses, only the 23 students who completed all questionnaires were used, and about half were female.
scenes.layout_description: A small group of 23 figures is shown, with one half lightly highlighted.
scenes.visual_prompt: Twenty-three tiny student figures in a cluster, with roughly half highlighted in orange.

scenes.narration: Most students reported no or little experience with time management strategies before training, which the authors note may matter for the results.
scenes.layout_description: A simple experience scale shows most marks near the low end.
scenes.visual_prompt: A horizontal experience scale with most markers clustered at the low end and one small marker higher up.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress was measured with the tension scale, perceived control of time with a ten-item scale, and demands with another five-item scale.
scenes.layout_description: Three stacked measurement cards show the three named scales.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three clean cards with icons: a tense face, a clock, and a stack of duties, each with small item dots.

scenes.narration: At time 1, time management behaviour related positively to perceived control of time, and perceived control of time related negatively to stress and demands.
scenes.layout_description: A small network diagram links the four study variables with arrows and signs.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal network of four circles labeled with icons, connected by arrows and plus or minus marks.

scenes.narration: After training, reported use of the taught strategies increased significantly by 4 weeks, and the 2-week increase was nearly significant.
scenes.layout_description: An upward arrow rises from a baseline to two later points on a simple chart.
scenes.visual_prompt: A minimalist line chart with an upward trend and highlighted points at baseline, 2 weeks, and 4 weeks.

scenes.narration: For the main outcomes, the repeated-measurement analysis showed a significant overall time effect after 2 weeks and a significant stress effect.
scenes.layout_description: Two outcome bars appear beside a small statistical symbol and arrows indicating change.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple chart with two bars or lines, one for stress dropping and one for control rising, with a small star marker.

scenes.narration: Two weeks after training, trainees reported significantly less stress, while perceived control of time showed only a tendency in the expected direction.
scenes.layout_description: A downward stress arrow and a faint upward clock arrow sit side by side.
scenes.visual_prompt: A stress gauge dropping downward and a clock icon with a faint upward arrow, both in black ink with orange highlights.

scenes.narration: Four weeks after training, both outcomes changed significantly: stress was lower and perceived control of time was higher than before training.
scenes.layout_description: Two bold arrows point in opposite directions from the pretest to the follow-up point.
scenes.visual_prompt: A before-and-after sketch with a stress cloud shrinking and a clock gaining a bright yellow halo.

scenes.narration: The control variable, demands, did not change significantly at either follow-up, which fits the study’s design.
scenes.layout_description: A flat line for demands runs beneath the changing outcome lines.
scenes.visual_prompt: A steady horizontal line labeled with a duty stack icon, while nearby lines move up and down.

scenes.narration: The authors say the pattern supports the conclusion that training reduced perceived stress and increased perceived control of time.
scenes.layout_description: A conclusion box gathers the two outcome arrows into one central statement shape.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two arrows, one down and one up, converge toward a central checkmark-like symbol.

scenes.narration: They also say the effects were very strong and practically relevant, even though the intervention lasted only 4 h.
scenes.layout_description: A short training block is shown beside a bold impact symbol.
scenes.visual_prompt: A small 4 h clock beside a large impact burst around a student and checklist.

scenes.narration: Students with no or little experience seemed to profit more than those with moderate or some experience, especially for perceived stress.
scenes.layout_description: Two student groups are shown, with the less experienced group highlighted more brightly.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two small groups of students, one with stronger orange highlights and larger arrows showing greater change.

scenes.narration: The authors suggest that prioritizing, goal setting, daily planning, and monitoring may give students more orientation and reduce stress.
scenes.layout_description: A path with signposts leads from confusion to a clear destination.
scenes.visual_prompt: A student walking along a simple path with signposts labeled by icons for goals, planning, and monitoring.

scenes.narration: They also note that monitoring can show completed tasks, creating reinforcing information that might help stress levels.
scenes.layout_description: A checklist fills with ticks, and a small glow appears around it.
scenes.visual_prompt: Checklist with several orange check marks and a small yellow glow around the completed items.

scenes.narration: Methodologically, the authors argue that the unchanged demands variable helps rule out testing, history, and placebo effects.
scenes.layout_description: A shield-like shape stands between the training and the control variable.
scenes.visual_prompt: A shield icon protecting the flat demands line while arrows point toward the changing outcomes.

scenes.narration: They also checked training transfer, and trainees reported more frequent use of the taught strategies after training than before.
scenes.layout_description: A hand moves a strategy card from the training side to daily life side.
scenes.visual_prompt: A student carrying a small toolbox of time strategies from a classroom into a daily schedule scene.

scenes.narration: The authors call the study preliminary because the sample was small and about half the students dropped out before the second measurement.
scenes.layout_description: A small group shrinks along a timeline toward later measurements.
scenes.visual_prompt: A timeline with student figures thinning out toward the later points, emphasizing dropout.

scenes.narration: They recommend more studies with larger samples, comparisons with other stress interventions, and tests of whether effects last longer.
scenes.layout_description: Three future research paths branch from one central study icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: A branching path diagram from one study page to three future directions, each with a simple icon.

scenes.narration: Overall, the paper suggests that time management training may help students feel more in control and less stressed, especially when they are new to it.
scenes.layout_description: A final balanced scene shows a calmer student beside a clock and checklist.
scenes.visual_prompt: A calm student with a small clock and checklist, surrounded by subtle orange and yellow accents, on a clean cream background.
